lesson.title: Follow the outside edge
lesson.subtitle: P4 measurement revision
lesson.objective: Find the outside boundary of a corner-cutout shape.
lesson.story: An outer 16 cm by 12 cm rectangle has a 2 cm by 2 cm corner removed.

steps.title: Find an outside segment
steps.prompt: The 2 cm corner length is removed from 16 cm across. Find the remaining horizontal outside segment in centimetres.
hints: Subtract the removed corner width from the outer width.

steps.title: Choose an outside-edge path
steps.prompt: Which paths count this corner-cutout's outside boundary?

choices.label: Add each outside edge in turn, leaving out any inside split lines.
Use 2 × (outer width + outer height); new edges replace equal lengths.
Add every drawn line, including the inside split line, all the way round.

hints: An inside split is not on the outline.
For this corner cutout only, new edge lengths replace the removed outer lengths.
Outside-edge sum and 2 × (outer width + outer height) agree for this shape.

steps.title: Find the outside boundary
steps.prompt: Find the perimeter of this 16 cm by 12 cm outer rectangle with one 2 cm by 2 cm corner removed. Answer in centimetres.
hints: One remaining horizontal segment is 14 cm.
The two new corner edges replace equal removed outer lengths.

steps.title: Explain the measure

choices.label: Area and perimeter are both measured in the same units.
An inside split line also counts as part of the perimeter.
Area counts square units; perimeter is only the outside edge.

hints: Look at what is being measured.
Area covers a surface; perimeter goes around its boundary.
An inside teaching split is not an outside edge.
Choose the explanation that separates square units from boundary length.
